# Game Boy Opcodes

> A searchable reference for the Game Boy instruction set, with machine-readable opcode data for emulator builders and developers.

The website explores the Sharp LR35902 instruction set. The supplied dataset contains 501 entries: 245 base instructions and 256 CB-prefixed instructions. The interface supports search, instruction group filters, grid and list views, an instruction inspector, JSON download, an offline HTML reference, and printing or saving as PDF.

## Primary resources

- [Opcode dataset](https://gb.insertcoin.dev/opcodes.json): The complete JSON dataset. Prefer this over extracting data from the interactive page.
- [Interactive explorer](https://gb.insertcoin.dev/): Browse both opcode tables, inspect instruction bytes and flags, and download or print the reference.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/lmmendes/game-boy-opcodes): Project source and history.
- [Report a data issue](https://github.com/lmmendes/game-boy-opcodes/issues): Report suspected errors in the supplied data.

## Dataset format

The JSON object has two top-level keys: `unprefixed` and `cbprefixed`. Each maps hexadecimal opcode keys such as `0x00` to instruction objects.

Instruction fields:

- `mnemonic`: Instruction name, such as `LD` or `NOP`.
- `operand1`, `operand2`: Optional operand strings, in assembly order.
- `length`: Instruction length in bytes, including the CB prefix where applicable.
- `cycles`: An array of timings in T-cycles. The viewer presents conditional timings in taken / not-taken order. One M-cycle equals four T-cycles.
- `flags`: Four strings in Z, N, H, C order (zero, subtract, half carry, carry). `-` means unchanged, `0` means cleared, `1` means set, and a letter means the result determines the flag.
- `addr`: Hexadecimal opcode address within its table. CB-prefixed entries require the leading `0xCB` byte in the instruction encoding.
- `group`: The supplied instruction classification: `x8/lsm`, `x16/lsm`, `x8/alu`, `x16/alu`, `x8/rsb`, `control/br`, or `control/misc`.

Operand notation used by the viewer includes `d8` / `d16` for immediate data, `a8` / `a16` for addresses, `r8` for signed relative offsets, and parentheses for memory operands.

## Interpretation

The explorer displays `opcodes.json` as supplied, including its classifications and timing values. It is a data reference, not a CPU simulator. Missing opcode addresses are absent from this dataset; do not invent entries for them. When reporting an instruction, identify its table as well as its opcode, and distinguish dataset values from independently verified hardware behavior.

Instruction links use fragments such as `https://gb.insertcoin.dev/#base-3e` and `https://gb.insertcoin.dev/#cb-00`.
